fills.researcher_notes: This is one of ten rows in the gtsou-core-operator brief, all inside government-controlled Ukraine (or, for cross-border rows, their Ukrainian section). Since 1 Jan 2020 the certified transmission system operator is Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC (ТОВ «Оператор ГТС України», GTSOU), unbundled from Ukrtransgaz/Naftogaz under the Energy Community-mandated unbundling law signed 15 Nov 2019 (company founded 4 Feb 2019, took over technical operation 1 Jul 2019, certified as the independent operator 1 Jan 2020). Verified via (1) ENTSOG's own European gas-TSO membership directory, which lists "LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine" as the Ukrainian member/observer TSO, and (2) Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated GTSOU article, an independent source giving the exact Ukrainian legal name and the full unbundling timeline. These are two independent origins (an industry association's own directory vs. an encyclopedia article), both verified OK, so tier=high. This answer was established once for the whole brief and is applied here rather than re-derived per row. utg.ua and tsoua.com (GTSOU's own site) both 403 to url_verifier -- a WAF block, not a deletion -- so the operator's own site was not needed as primary evidence; ENTSOG + uk.wikipedia stand on their own. This does NOT extend to occupied-territory or wholly Russian-side pipe, which are out of this brief's scope. This row is the Vojany-Uzhgorod line, cross-border Slovakia→Ukraine (the 2014 reverse-flow interconnector). The GTSOU answer above covers the Ukrainian section. For the Slovak section, eustream, a.s. is confirmed as the Slovak gas transmission system operator by two independent sources: ENTSOG's own membership directory (which lists "eustream, a.s." as the Slovak member TSO) and eustream's own company-profile page ("As the operator of the natural gas transmission network in the Slovak Republic...", and noting its network connects into Ukraine among other neighbours). Neither source names the Vojany-Uzhhorod line by name specifically -- both confirm eustream's role at the Slovak-TSO / Ukraine-interconnection level rather than this exact pipeline -- so the eustream half of the value is proposed at medium strength; combined with the high-tier GTSOU half, the joint value is proposed at tier=medium overall. [Leg-3 review 2026-08-15] Independence check: the pair originally cited here was ENTSOG's member list plus a Ukrainian-language Wikipedia article, and a tertiary encyclopaedia is not a second independent ORIGIN under the project's tier rules. Added GTSOU's own 'Key facts' page (Wayback 2020-06-03, live origin 403s behind the operator WAF), which states the legal name 'Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC' outright. The high tier therefore rests on ENTSOG (third-party European TSO association) + the operator's own primary statement; the Wikipedia link is retained as a reading aid and is NOT counted toward independence.
